label: First input token, for a fixed subset of 17 tokens (a c d e g h k l m o r t w x z 2 3)
explanation: Update-gate unit that fires at step 0 (the first original token) if and only if that token is one of a fixed set of 17: a c d e g h k l m o r t w x z 2 3. Each of these fires on every sequence that starts with it (dev precision 1.0 per token), and none of the other 13 tokens (b f i j n p q s u v y 0 1) ever fires at step 0. Magnitude depends on which token it is: 3 is strongest (it reaches the max), z/o/r/l are high, and a/g/t/w are weakest. About 4% of activation mass sits outside step 0. These are weak firings at steps 1-4 of the original phase on the first occurrence of a token from the same set (for example z after a leading i/s/n/u). There are almost no firings in the copy phase and none on <DEL>. Position later than t=0 almost completely shuts it off.

issues: The misses (about 8.7% of active steps, 3.7% of mass) form one consistent class, not random noise: weak firings at t=1-4 on the first token from the 17-token set. These follow leading tokens outside the set or occur in the copy phase at recall_idx=1. The explanation already describes this class.

I tried widening the predicate to the first occurrence of a set token anywhere in the original phase (n_seen==0). Recall rose to 0.99, but precision fell to 0.62-0.67, giving test F1 0.76-0.80. Most such later occurrences do not fire, so the t==0 predicate remains the better one.

Verified: none of the 13 tokens outside the set ever fires at t=0 (precision 0). There are no false positives on the test split, so each of the 17 tokens fires every time it starts a sequence. The unit never fires on <DEL> and almost never in the copy phase (236 steps on dev). The per-token strength ordering fits the profile (3 is strongest, then z/o/r/l).
